title: Police shoot an armed man in west Edmonton Sunday morning
article: A man shot by Edmonton police is in hospital with serious injuries.
At around 4 a.m. Sunday, West Division police officers responded to a 911 call near 85 Avenue and 149 Street regarding a man who was threatening to shoot himself.
According to police, when officers arrived they were approached by a 50-year-old man with a long-barreled weapon.
One officer shot the man, who remains in hospital for the treatment of serious but non-life threatening injuries.
The man was given medical attention and taken to hospital, where he required surgery.
A neighbour said he watched police attend to the man outside after he was woken up by gunshots Sunday morning in the typically calm neighbourhood.
He described the shooting victim as "a pretty kind guy" who is usually quiet.
The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT), which investigates all officer involved shootings, has taken over the investigation.
Meanwhile, police are investigating another early morning shooting in southwest Edmonton.
Police and EMS responded to a "trouble not known" call at a home near Graham Wynd and 199 Street just before 5 a.m. Sunday, where emergency responders found a female with a gunshot wound.
EMS treated the victim and took her to hospital, where she remains in serious but stable condition.
Police continue to investigate, and are asking anyone who may have seen suspicious activity in the area between 3 a.m. and 5 a.m. to call EPS at 780-423-4567 or contact Crime Stoppers.
